rationale:
Split. The selected theorem bundles six independent, reusable obligations that its supplied proof uses. (1) A smooth Urysohn cutoff ζ (step 1). (2) The Leibniz estimate for D^i(ζω) (step 4). (3) Sequential continuity of ω ↦ ζω from 𝒟^k(ℝ^P) to 𝒟^k(U) (steps 2 and 4). (4) Homogeneity |cα| = |c||α| of the coefficient norm (step 3). (5) Lifting an IMRep whose carrier lies in K to ℝ^P (step 11). (6) spt ⊆ K for a current that vanishes off K (step 9).

Item (2) is critical. Step 4 cites Mathlib's norm_iteratedFDeriv_smul_le, which lives in Mathlib.Analysis.Calculus.ContDiff.Bounds. That file is not in the frozen import closure: after `import GMT.Ch07.Submission` the identifier is unknown, and the header may not change. The estimate therefore has to be re-proved. It becomes its own child with a complete bilinear-induction proof. That proof uses an explicit constant c instead of ‖B‖, because the operator-norm instance on doubly nested spaces of continuous linear maps fails to synthesize under the project's default maxSynthPendingDepth. Leaves must be single theorems with no set_option (leaf_lean_agent_review = false).

Items (4) and (6) reuse comparator-accepted declarations with byte-identical frozen types: rsd_mw_tfa_norm_props and rsd_cmr_support_subset_of_vanish. Both are accepted with candidate commits.

After the split the parent is a short assembly (about 115 Lean lines):
- Take (ζ, N) from smooth_cutoff. Take M₁ := cutoff_multiplier at degree m+1 and M₀ at degree m.
- Set E X := X ∘ M₁. It is continuous by M₁'s continuity and X.continuous'.
- (i) ζω = ω when tsupport ω ⊆ K.
- (ii) Holds pointwise.
- (iii) M₁ maps admissible forms to admissible forms, by norm_props (ii) and 0 ≤ ζ ≤ 1.
- (iv) Apply support_of_vanishing with U := univ to E X. For the boundary mass, δ := d(M₀η) − M₁(dη) vanishes on N by Filter.EventuallyEq.extDeriv_eq. So X(δ) = 0 and ∂(E X)(η) = ∂X(M₀η), with M₀η admissible.
- (v) Use imrep_lift plus setIntegral_congr_fun on the carrier, where ζ = 1.

subproblems.title: Smooth cutoff with compact support in U equal to 1 on an open neighbourhood of a compact K ⊆ U
subproblems.statement: Let P ∈ ℕ, let U ⊆ ℝ^P be open and K ⊆ U compact. Then there are a function ζ : ℝ^P → ℝ and a set N ⊆ ℝ^P such that ζ is C^∞ (ContDiff ℝ ∞), ζ has compact support, tsupport ζ ⊆ U, 0 ≤ ζ(x) ≤ 1 for every x ∈ ℝ^P, N is open, K ⊆ N, and ζ(x) = 1 for every x ∈ N.
subproblems.lean_statement: ∀ (P : ℕ) (U K : Set (Euclid P)), IsOpen U → IsCompact K → K ⊆ U → ∃ (ζ : Euclid P → ℝ) (N : Set (Euclid P)), ContDiff ℝ (⊤ : ℕ∞) ζ ∧ HasCompactSupport ζ ∧ tsupport ζ ⊆ U ∧ (∀ x, 0 ≤ ζ x ∧ ζ x ≤ 1) ∧ IsOpen N ∧ K ⊆ N ∧ ∀ x ∈ N, ζ x = 1
subproblems.natural_proof:
Source: the parent-supplied proof of cbrcs_cutoff_extension, step 1 (Cutoff), isolated for an arbitrary open U and compact K ⊆ U.

1. (First neighbourhood.) ℝ^P = Euclid P is a finite-dimensional real normed space, hence locally compact and regular. Since K is compact, U is open and K ⊆ U, Mathlib's exists_open_between_and_isCompact_closure gives an open set V₁ with K ⊆ V₁, closure V₁ ⊆ U and closure V₁ compact.
2. (Second neighbourhood.) closure V₁ is a compact subset of the open set U, so the same lemma gives an open set V₂ with closure V₁ ⊆ V₂, closure V₂ ⊆ U and closure V₂ compact.
3. (Smooth Urysohn function.) closure V₁ is closed (isClosed_closure), V₂ is open and closure V₁ ⊆ V₂. Mathlib's exists_contDiff_support_eq_eq_one_iff (in the finite-dimensional real normed space ℝ^P, with smoothness order (⊤ : ℕ∞), i.e. C^∞, s := V₂, t := closure V₁) yields ζ : ℝ^P → ℝ with ContDiff ℝ ∞ ζ, range ζ ⊆ [0, 1], support ζ = V₂, and, for every x, x ∈ closure V₁ ↔ ζ(x) = 1.
4. (Topological support.) tsupport ζ = closure (support ζ) = closure V₂. By step 2 this set is compact, so ζ has compact support (HasCompactSupport ζ is exactly compactness of tsupport ζ), and tsupport ζ = closure V₂ ⊆ U.
5. (Values.) For every x, ζ(x) ∈ range ζ ⊆ [0, 1], so 0 ≤ ζ(x) and ζ(x) ≤ 1.
6. (The open set N.) Put N := V₁. N is open and K ⊆ N by step 1. If x ∈ N then x ∈ closure V₁ (subset_closure), so ζ(x) = 1 by the forward direction of the equivalence in step 3.
7. (Conclusion.) Steps 3–6 show that (ζ, N) has all required properties: ζ is C^∞ (step 3), has compact support and tsupport ζ ⊆ U (step 4), 0 ≤ ζ ≤ 1 (step 5), and N is open with K ⊆ N and ζ = 1 on N (step 6). ∎

Lean note (checked against the frozen imports, single theorem, no helper declarations): exists_open_between_and_isCompact_closure hK hU hKU, then exists_open_between_and_isCompact_closure hV₁compact hU hV₁U, then exists_contDiff_support_eq_eq_one_iff (n := (⊤ : ℕ∞)) hV₂open isClosed_closure hV₁V₂ (its order argument has type ℕ∞ in this Mathlib and its conclusion is ContDiff ℝ ↑⊤ ζ); rw [tsupport, hsupport] rewrites tsupport ζ to closure V₂.
proof_key_steps: Two applications of exists_open_between_and_isCompact_closure give open V₁ ⊇ K and V₂ ⊇ closure V₁ with closure V₂ compact and contained in U.
The smooth Urysohn lemma exists_contDiff_support_eq_eq_one_iff (order ∞, s := V₂, t := closure V₁) gives ζ with values in [0,1], support ζ = V₂ and ζ = 1 exactly on closure V₁.
tsupport ζ = closure V₂ is compact and contained in U; N := V₁ is open, contains K, and ζ = 1 on N.

subproblems.title: Leibniz estimate for the iterated derivatives of a scalar function times a differential form
subproblems.statement: Let P, k, n ∈ ℕ, let f : ℝ^P → ℝ and g : ℝ^P → Λ^k(ℝ^P) (a k-form, DifferentialForm (Euclid P) k, i.e. a map into the continuous alternating k-linear forms on ℝ^P with their operator norm) both be C^∞, and let x ∈ ℝ^P. Then ‖D^n(f g)(x)‖ ≤ Σ_{i=0}^{n} C(n,i)·‖D^i f(x)‖·‖D^{n−i} g(x)‖, where f g is the form y ↦ f(y)·g(y), D^i = iteratedFDeriv ℝ i, C(n,i) is the binomial coefficient and ‖·‖ is the operator norm of continuous multilinear maps.
subproblems.lean_statement: ∀ (P k n : ℕ) (f : Euclid P → ℝ) (g : DifferentialForm (Euclid P) k) (x : Euclid P), ContDiff ℝ (⊤ : ℕ∞) f → ContDiff ℝ (⊤ : ℕ∞) g → ‖iteratedFDeriv ℝ n (fun y => f y • g y) x‖ ≤ ∑ i ∈ Finset.range (n + 1), (n.choose i : ℝ) * ‖iteratedFDeriv ℝ i f x‖ * ‖iteratedFDeriv ℝ (n - i) g x‖
subproblems.natural_proof:
Source: the Leibniz estimate invoked in step 4 of the parent-supplied proof of cbrcs_cutoff_extension (there cited as Mathlib norm_iteratedFDeriv_smul_le). That Mathlib lemma lives in Mathlib.Analysis.Calculus.ContDiff.Bounds, which is not in the import closure of the frozen contract (checked: the identifier is unknown after import GMT.Ch07.Submission), so the estimate is proved here by the same bilinear induction as Mathlib's ContinuousLinearMap.norm_iteratedFDerivWithin_le_of_bilinear_aux (that lemma is also in the non-imported Bounds file; it is cited only as the model of the induction and is not used), written with an explicit bilinear constant c.

Notation. Write D := ℝ^P, fix x ∈ D, and for a map h from D to a real normed space write D^i h(x) := iteratedFDeriv ℝ i h x and Dh := fderiv ℝ h. All spaces below are real normed spaces in Type (as D and the covector space are).

1. (Generalized claim.) For n ∈ ℕ let (A_n) be the statement: for all real normed spaces E, F, G, every continuous bilinear map B : E →L F →L G, every real c ≥ 0 with ‖B u v‖ ≤ c·‖u‖·‖v‖ for all u ∈ E, v ∈ F, and all C^∞ maps a : D → E and b : D → F,
   ‖D^n(y ↦ B (a y) (b y))(x)‖ ≤ c · Σ_{i=0}^{n} C(n,i)·‖D^i a(x)‖·‖D^{n−i} b(x)‖.
   We prove (A_n) for every n by induction on n; the spaces E, F, G, the map B, the constant c and the maps a, b are universally quantified inside (A_n), because the induction step applies (A_n) to different spaces.
2. (Base case n = 0.) ‖D^0 h(x)‖ = ‖h(x)‖ for every h (norm_iteratedFDeriv_zero), and the right-hand side of (A_0) is c·C(0,0)·‖a(x)‖·‖b(x)‖ = c·‖a(x)‖·‖b(x)‖. So (A_0) is the hypothesis ‖B (a x) (b x)‖ ≤ c·‖a x‖·‖b x‖.
3. (Induction step: setup.) Assume (A_n). Let E, F, G, B, c, a, b be as in (A_{n+1}) and put h(y) := B (a y) (b y). Since a and b are C^∞, so are Da and Db (ContDiff.fderiv_right with order ∞).
4. (Two auxiliary bilinear maps.) Let B₁ := B.precompR D : E →L (D →L F) →L (D →L G), B₁ u L = (v ↦ B u (L v)), and B₂ := B.precompL D : (D →L E) →L F →L (D →L G), B₂ L w = (v ↦ B (L v) w). For all u, L and v: ‖B u (L v)‖ ≤ c·‖u‖·‖L v‖ ≤ c·‖u‖·‖L‖·‖v‖, hence ‖B₁ u L‖ ≤ c·‖u‖·‖L‖ by the operator-norm bound (opNorm_le_bound, c·‖u‖·‖L‖ ≥ 0). Likewise ‖B (L v) w‖ ≤ c·‖L v‖·‖w‖ ≤ c·‖L‖·‖w‖·‖v‖ gives ‖B₂ L w‖ ≤ c·‖L‖·‖w‖. So B₁ and B₂ satisfy the hypothesis of (A_n) with the same constant c.
5. (Product rule.) By the derivative of a bilinear expression (ContinuousLinearMap.fderiv_of_bilinear, a and b differentiable), for every y: Dh(y) = B₁ (a y) (Db y) + B₂ (Da y) (b y).
6. (Splitting the derivative.) The maps y ↦ B₁ (a y) (Db y) and y ↦ B₂ (Da y) (b y) are C^∞ (a bounded bilinear map is C^∞, composed with the C^∞ pairs (a, Db) and (Da, b)). Hence D^n of their sum at x is the sum of their D^n at x (iteratedFDeriv_add_apply). Using ‖D^{n+1} h(x)‖ = ‖D^n(Dh)(x)‖ (norm_iteratedFDeriv_fderiv), step 5 and the triangle inequality,
   ‖D^{n+1} h(x)‖ ≤ ‖D^n(y ↦ B₁ (a y) (Db y))(x)‖ + ‖D^n(y ↦ B₂ (Da y) (b y))(x)‖.
7. (First term.) (A_n) for (E, D →L F, D →L G, B₁, c, a, Db) gives ‖D^n(B₁(a, Db))(x)‖ ≤ c·Σ_{i=0}^{n} C(n,i)·‖D^i a(x)‖·‖D^{n−i}(Db)(x)‖. By norm_iteratedFDeriv_fderiv, ‖D^{n−i}(Db)(x)‖ = ‖D^{n−i+1} b(x)‖, and n − i + 1 = n + 1 − i for i ≤ n. So the first term is ≤ c·Σ_{i=0}^{n} C(n,i)·‖D^i a(x)‖·‖D^{n+1−i} b(x)‖.
8. (Second term.) (A_n) for (D →L E, F, D →L G, B₂, c, Da, b) gives ‖D^n(B₂(Da, b))(x)‖ ≤ c·Σ_{i=0}^{n} C(n,i)·‖D^i(Da)(x)‖·‖D^{n−i} b(x)‖ = c·Σ_{i=0}^{n} C(n,i)·‖D^{i+1} a(x)‖·‖D^{n−i} b(x)‖ (norm_iteratedFDeriv_fderiv again).
9. (Pascal's rule.) For φ(i, j) := ‖D^i a(x)‖·‖D^j b(x)‖, Finset.sum_choose_succ_mul states Σ_{i=0}^{n+1} C(n+1,i)·φ(i, n+1−i) = Σ_{i=0}^{n} C(n,i)·φ(i, n+1−i) + Σ_{i=0}^{n} C(n,i)·φ(i+1, n−i). Adding the bounds of steps 7 and 8 and factoring out c therefore gives ‖D^{n+1} h(x)‖ ≤ c·Σ_{i=0}^{n+1} C(n+1,i)·‖D^i a(x)‖·‖D^{n+1−i} b(x)‖, which is (A_{n+1}).
10. (Specialization.) Apply (A_n) with E := ℝ, F = G := Covector (Euclid P) k, B := ContinuousLinearMap.lsmul ℝ ℝ (so B t v = t • v), c := 1, a := f, b := g. The hypothesis holds because ‖t • v‖ = |t|·‖v‖ = 1·‖t‖·‖v‖, and B (f y) (g y) = f y • g y. Since 1·Σ = Σ, this is exactly the claimed inequality. ∎

Lean note (verified to compile as one theorem under the frozen imports, axioms propext, Classical.choice, Quot.sound): the leaf must be a single theorem without helper declarations or set_option. Prove (A_n) inside it as have aux : ∀ (n : ℕ) (E F G : Type) [NormedAddCommGroup E] [NormedSpace ℝ E] [NormedAddCommGroup F] [NormedSpace ℝ F] [NormedAddCommGroup G] [NormedSpace ℝ G] (B : E →L[ℝ] F →L[ℝ] G) (c : ℝ) (a : Euclid P → E) (b : Euclid P → F), 0 ≤ c → (∀ u v, ‖B u v‖ ≤ c * ‖u‖ * ‖v‖) → ContDiff ℝ (⊤ : ℕ∞) a → ContDiff ℝ (⊤ : ℕ∞) b → ‖iteratedFDeriv ℝ n (fun y => B (a y) (b y)) x‖ ≤ c * ∑ i ∈ Finset.range (n + 1), (n.choose i : ℝ) * ‖iteratedFDeriv ℝ i a x‖ * ‖iteratedFDeriv ℝ (n - i) b x‖ := by intro n; induction n with ... . Use the explicit constant c, not ‖B‖: elaborating ‖B.precompR (Euclid P)‖ needs the operator norm on a doubly nested space of continuous linear maps, which fails to synthesize under the project default maxSynthPendingDepth (Mathlib itself builds with 3). Useful names: norm_iteratedFDeriv_zero, norm_iteratedFDeriv_fderiv, ContinuousLinearMap.precompR_apply, ContinuousLinearMap.compL_apply, ContinuousLinearMap.precompL_apply, ContinuousLinearMap.opNorm_le_bound, ContinuousLinearMap.le_opNorm, ContinuousLinearMap.fderiv_of_bilinear, (B.precompR _).isBoundedBilinearMap.contDiff.comp₂, fun_iteratedFDeriv_add_apply, Finset.sum_choose_succ_mul, Finset.sum_add_distrib, ContinuousLinearMap.lsmul.
proof_key_steps: Generalize to a continuous bilinear B with ‖B u v‖ ≤ c‖u‖‖v‖ and prove ‖D^n B(a,b)(x)‖ ≤ c Σ C(n,i)‖D^i a(x)‖‖D^{n−i} b(x)‖ by induction on n, quantifying over the target spaces.
Base case: the hypothesis on B at (a x, b x).
Step: ‖D^{n+1}h(x)‖ = ‖D^n(Dh)(x)‖ and Dh = B.precompR(a, Db) + B.precompL(Da, b), both bilinear maps again bounded by c.
Apply the induction hypothesis to both terms, convert D^j(Db), D^j(Da) to D^{j+1}b, D^{j+1}a, and combine with Pascal's rule Finset.sum_choose_succ_mul.
Specialize to B = lsmul, c = 1, a = f, b = g.

subproblems.title: Multiplication by a compactly supported smooth function is a sequentially continuous linear map from 𝒟^k(ℝ^P) to 𝒟^k(U)
subproblems.statement: Let P, k ∈ ℕ, let U ⊆ ℝ^P be any set and let ζ : ℝ^P → ℝ be C^∞ with compact support and tsupport ζ ⊆ U. Then there is an ℝ-linear map M : 𝒟^k(ℝ^P) → 𝒟^k(U) (TestFormOn univ k →ₗ[ℝ] TestFormOn U k) with (Mω)(x) = ζ(x)·ω(x) for every ω ∈ 𝒟^k(ℝ^P) and every x ∈ ℝ^P, such that for every sequence ω_j in 𝒟^k(ℝ^P) with ω_j → 0 in the test-form topology (TestFormOnConverges ω_j 0: one compact set contains all tsupport ω_j and every iterated derivative converges uniformly on it) we have Mω_j → 0 in 𝒟^k(U) (TestFormOnConverges (Mω_j) 0).
subproblems.lean_statement: ∀ (P k : ℕ) (U : Set (Euclid P)) (ζ : Euclid P → ℝ), ContDiff ℝ (⊤ : ℕ∞) ζ → HasCompactSupport ζ → tsupport ζ ⊆ U → ∃ M : TestFormOn (univ : Set (Euclid P)) k →ₗ[ℝ] TestFormOn U k, (∀ (ω : TestFormOn (univ : Set (Euclid P)) k) (x : Euclid P), (M ω : DifferentialForm (Euclid P) k) x = ζ x • (ω : DifferentialForm (Euclid P) k) x) ∧ ∀ ωs : ℕ → TestFormOn (univ : Set (Euclid P)) k, TestFormOnConverges ωs 0 → TestFormOnConverges (fun j => M (ωs j)) 0
subproblems.natural_proof:
Source: the parent-supplied proof of cbrcs_cutoff_extension, steps 2 (multiplication by ζ) and 4 (continuity of M_k), for an arbitrary compactly supported C^∞ function ζ with tsupport ζ ⊆ U. The Leibniz estimate is the sibling leibniz_bound (Lean cbrcs_ce_leibniz_smul_bound).

1. (ζω is a test form in U.) Let ω ∈ 𝒟^k(ℝ^P), so ω is C^∞ with compact support (membership in TestFormOn univ k is IsTestForm ω ∧ tsupport ω ⊆ univ). Let ζω := (x ↦ ζ(x)·ω(x)). (a) ζω is C^∞, as a product of C^∞ maps (ContDiff.smul). (b) support(ζω) ⊆ support ζ, so ζω has compact support because ζ does (HasCompactSupport.smul_right). (c) tsupport(ζω) ⊆ tsupport ζ ⊆ U (tsupport_smul_subset_left). Hence ζω ∈ 𝒟^k(U).
2. (Linearity.) Define M ω := ζω ∈ 𝒟^k(U), using step 1. For ω, η and c ∈ ℝ, pointwise ζ(x)·(ω(x) + η(x)) = ζ(x)·ω(x) + ζ(x)·η(x) (smul_add) and ζ(x)·(c·ω(x)) = c·(ζ(x)·ω(x)) (smul_comm); by extensionality of the subtype (Subtype.ext, funext), M(ω + η) = Mω + Mη and M(cω) = c·Mω. By construction (Mω)(x) = ζ(x)·ω(x) for all ω and x, which is the required formula.
3. (Continuity: the compact set.) Let ω_j → 0 in 𝒟^k(ℝ^P): there is a compact K′ with tsupport ω_j ⊆ K′ for all j and, for every l ∈ ℕ, D^l ω_j → D^l 0 uniformly on K′ (D^l := iteratedFDeriv ℝ l). The coercion of 0 ∈ 𝒟^k(·) is the zero form, and D^l of the zero function is 0 (iteratedFDeriv_zero). We prove TestFormOnConverges (Mω_j) 0 with the compact set K₂ := tsupport ζ: it is compact (HasCompactSupport ζ), K₂ ⊆ U, tsupport(Mω_j) = tsupport(ζω_j) ⊆ tsupport ζ = K₂ for all j (tsupport_smul_subset_left), and tsupport of the zero form is ∅ ⊆ K₂. It remains to show, for every i ∈ ℕ, that D^i(Mω_j) → 0 uniformly on K₂.
4. (Bounds on the derivatives of ζ.) For each l ∈ ℕ, D^l ζ is continuous (ContDiff.continuous_iteratedFDeriv, l ≤ ∞) and has compact support (HasCompactSupport.iteratedFDeriv), hence is bounded: there is B_l ∈ ℝ with ‖D^l ζ(x)‖ ≤ B_l for all x (Continuous.bounded_above_of_compact_support). Put B_l⁺ := max(B_l, 0) ≥ 0.
5. (The derivatives of ω_j are uniformly small on all of ℝ^P.) Fix l ∈ ℕ and δ > 0. By uniform convergence on K′ (Metric.tendstoUniformlyOn_iff), for all sufficiently large j we have ‖D^l ω_j(x)‖ = dist(0, D^l ω_j(x)) < δ for every x ∈ K′. If x ∉ K′, then x ∉ tsupport ω_j ⊆ K′, so D^l ω_j(x) = 0 because support(D^l ω_j) ⊆ tsupport ω_j (support_iteratedFDeriv_subset), and ‖D^l ω_j(x)‖ = 0 < δ. Hence, eventually in j, ‖D^l ω_j(x)‖ < δ for all x ∈ ℝ^P.
6. (Leibniz estimate.) Fix i ∈ ℕ and ε > 0. Put C := Σ_{l=0}^{i} C(i,l)·B_l⁺ ≥ 0 and δ := ε/(C + 1) > 0. Applying step 5 to the finitely many orders i − l, l ∈ {0, …, i} (Filter.eventually_all_finset), for all sufficiently large j: ‖D^{i−l} ω_j(x)‖ < δ for all l ≤ i and all x. For such j and every x ∈ K₂, the sibling leibniz_bound applied to f := ζ and g := ω_j (both C^∞) gives
   ‖D^i(Mω_j)(x)‖ = ‖D^i(ζω_j)(x)‖ ≤ Σ_{l=0}^{i} C(i,l)·‖D^l ζ(x)‖·‖D^{i−l} ω_j(x)‖ ≤ Σ_{l=0}^{i} C(i,l)·B_l⁺·δ = C·δ = C·ε/(C + 1) < ε.
   Thus dist(D^i 0(x), D^i(Mω_j)(x)) = ‖D^i(Mω_j)(x)‖ < ε for all x ∈ K₂, for all large j; i.e. D^i(Mω_j) → 0 uniformly on K₂ (Metric.tendstoUniformlyOn_iff).
7. (Conclusion.) M is ℝ-linear with (Mω)(x) = ζ(x)·ω(x) (step 2), and whenever ω_j → 0 in 𝒟^k(ℝ^P), steps 3 and 6 verify every clause of TestFormOnConverges (Mω_j) 0 with the compact set K₂ = tsupport ζ ⊆ U. ∎

subproblems.title: The Euclidean coefficient norm of n-covectors is a continuous seminorm dominated by the operator norm
subproblems.statement: Let P, n ∈ ℕ, let F := Covector (Euclid P) n (continuous alternating n-linear forms on ℝ^P with the operator norm ‖·‖), and let N := covectorEuclideanNorm, i.e. N(α) = (Σ_{I : Fin n → Fin P strictly increasing} α(e_{I(0)}, …, e_{I(n−1)})²)^{1/2} for the standard orthonormal basis (e_j) of ℝ^P. Then (i) N(α + α') ≤ N(α) + N(α') for all α, α' ∈ F; (ii) N(t·α) = |t|·N(α) for all t ∈ ℝ and α ∈ F; (iii) there is a real C ≥ 0 with N(α) ≤ C·‖α‖ for all α ∈ F; and (iv) N : F → ℝ is continuous.
subproblems.lean_statement: ∀ (P n : ℕ), (∀ α α' : Covector (Euclid P) n, covectorEuclideanNorm (α + α') ≤ covectorEuclideanNorm α + covectorEuclideanNorm α') ∧ (∀ (t : ℝ) (α : Covector (Euclid P) n), covectorEuclideanNorm (t • α) = |t| * covectorEuclideanNorm α) ∧ (∃ C : ℝ, 0 ≤ C ∧ ∀ α : Covector (Euclid P) n, covectorEuclideanNorm α ≤ C * ‖α‖) ∧ Continuous (fun α : Covector (Euclid P) n => covectorEuclideanNorm α)
subproblems.natural_proof:
Reused comparator-accepted declaration rsd_mw_tfa_norm_props (DAG node root.regular_set_dense-a1.mass_eq_weight-a1.test_form_approx-a1.norm_props-a1, accepted with a candidate commit) with byte-identical frozen type; its accepted natural proof is reproduced verbatim below. The parent cbrcs_cutoff_extension uses only conjunct (ii), N(t·α) = |t|·N(α).

Source: parent proof, step 1 (Properties of N), with all details filled in.

Notation. e_j := EuclideanSpace.basisFun (Fin P) ℝ j (j ∈ Fin P) is the standard orthonormal basis of ℝ^P, so ‖e_j‖ = 1. 𝓙 is the finite type of all maps I : Fin n → Fin P, and #𝓙 = Fintype.card (Fin n → Fin P). For I ∈ 𝓙, e_I := (e_{I(0)}, …, e_{I(n−1)}), in Lean (fun i => e (I i)). F := Covector (Euclid P) n carries the operator norm ‖·‖ of continuous alternating maps. By definition
N(α) := covectorEuclideanNorm α = √(Σ_{I∈𝓙} q_I(α)), where q_I(α) := α(e_I)² if I is strictly increasing and q_I(α) := 0 otherwise.

1. Coefficient vector. For α ∈ F and I ∈ 𝓙 put c_I(α) := α(e_I) if I is strictly increasing, and c_I(α) := 0 otherwise. Since (if p then a else 0)² = (if p then a² else 0), q_I(α) = c_I(α)² for every I. Let v(α) ∈ EuclideanSpace ℝ 𝓙 be the vector with coordinates c_I(α); in Lean, v α := WithLp.toLp 2 (fun I => c_I α). The Euclidean norm formula ‖w‖ = √(Σ_I ‖w_I‖²) (EuclideanSpace.norm_eq), together with ‖w_I‖² = w_I², gives
   N(α) = ‖v(α)‖ for every α ∈ F.   (∗)

2. Linearity of v. Evaluation at a fixed tuple is linear in the form: (α + α')(e_I) = α(e_I) + α'(e_I) and (t·α)(e_I) = t·α(e_I). So, coordinatewise, c_I(α + α') = c_I(α) + c_I(α') and c_I(t·α) = t·c_I(α); both sides are 0 when I is not strictly increasing. Hence v(α + α') = v(α) + v(α') and v(t·α) = t·v(α) (WithLp.toLp_add, WithLp.toLp_smul).

3. Proof of (i). By (∗), step 2 and the triangle inequality in EuclideanSpace ℝ 𝓙:
   N(α + α') = ‖v(α) + v(α')‖ ≤ ‖v(α)‖ + ‖v(α')‖ = N(α) + N(α').

4. Proof of (ii). By (∗), step 2 and homogeneity of the norm:
   N(t·α) = ‖t·v(α)‖ = |t|·‖v(α)‖ = |t|·N(α).

5. Coordinate bound. For every I ∈ 𝓙, |c_I(α)| ≤ ‖α‖.
   - If I is strictly increasing, the operator-norm bound for continuous alternating maps (ContinuousAlternatingMap.le_opNorm) gives |α(e_I)| ≤ ‖α‖·∏_k ‖e_{I(k)}‖ = ‖α‖·1 = ‖α‖.
   - Otherwise |c_I(α)| = 0 ≤ ‖α‖.

6. Proof of (iii). Put C := √(#𝓙) ≥ 0. By step 5, c_I(α)² = |c_I(α)|² ≤ ‖α‖² for every I, so Σ_I c_I(α)² ≤ #𝓙·‖α‖². Since √ is monotone and ‖α‖ ≥ 0,
   N(α) = √(Σ_I c_I(α)²) ≤ √(#𝓙·‖α‖²) = √(#𝓙)·√(‖α‖²) = C·‖α‖.

7. Proof of (iv). Let α, α' ∈ F.
   - By (i), N(α) = N((α − α') + α') ≤ N(α − α') + N(α').
   - α' − α = −(α − α') and N(−β) = N(β) (covectorEuclideanNorm_neg, or (ii) with t = −1). So by (i), N(α') = N((α' − α) + α) ≤ N(α' − α) + N(α) = N(α − α') + N(α).
   Together with (iii), |N(α) − N(α')| ≤ N(α − α') ≤ C·‖α − α'‖. Thus dist(N(α), N(α')) ≤ C·dist(α, α') for all α, α', so N is Lipschitz with the nonnegative constant C (LipschitzWith.of_dist_le_mul with K := ⟨C, C ≥ 0⟩), hence continuous.

Steps 3, 4, 6 and 7 prove (i)–(iv), with the constant C of (iii) equal to √(Fintype.card (Fin n → Fin P)).

Lean note. A compiled route (about 70 lines, no extra imports):
- Use `classical`, and define c and v with `let`.
- Prove (∗) by `rw [EuclideanSpace.norm_eq]; unfold covectorEuclideanNorm; congr 1`, then `Finset.sum_congr rfl` with `by_cases hI : StrictMono I` and `simp`.
- Prove linearity by `simp only [v, ← WithLp.toLp_add]` (resp. `← WithLp.toLp_smul`), then `congr 1; funext I; by_cases hI : StrictMono I <;> simp [c, hI]`.
- For step 5, use `α.le_opNorm (fun i => e (I i))` followed by `simpa [Real.norm_eq_abs]`; simp knows that basis vectors have norm 1.
- For step 6, use `Real.sqrt_sq`, `Real.sqrt_mul`, `Real.sqrt_le_sqrt`, `Finset.sum_le_sum` and `pow_le_pow_left₀`.
- For step 7, first rewrite N(α' − α) = N(α − α') by `rw [← neg_sub, covectorEuclideanNorm_neg]`, then apply (i) together with `sub_add_cancel`, `abs_le` and `linarith`. Finish with `(LipschitzWith.of_dist_le_mul (K := ⟨_, Real.sqrt_nonneg _⟩) hlip).continuous`.
proof_key_steps: Write N(α) = ‖v(α)‖ for the coefficient vector v(α) = (α(e_I) if I is strictly increasing, else 0)_I in EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin n → Fin P).
v is additive and ℝ-homogeneous, because evaluation at a fixed tuple is linear in α.
(i) and (ii) follow from the triangle inequality and homogeneity of the Euclidean norm.
|α(e_I)| ≤ ‖α‖·∏‖e_{I(k)}‖ = ‖α‖, so N(α) ≤ √(card(Fin n → Fin P))·‖α‖, which is (iii).
|N(α) − N(α')| ≤ N(α − α') ≤ C‖α − α'‖, so N is Lipschitz and hence continuous, which is (iv).

subproblems.title: An integer multiplicity triple in U whose carrier lies in a compact K ⊆ U is a triple in ℝ^P
subproblems.statement: Let P, n ∈ ℕ, let U, K ⊆ ℝ^P with K compact and K ⊆ U, and let R = (M, θ, ξ) be an integer multiplicity triple in U (IMRep U n) with carrier M ⊆ K. Then there is an integer multiplicity triple R′ in ℝ^P (IMRep univ n) with the same carrier, multiplicity and orientation: R′.carrier = M, R′.mult = θ and R′.orient = ξ.
subproblems.lean_statement: ∀ (P n : ℕ) (U K : Set (Euclid P)) (R : IMRep U n), IsCompact K → K ⊆ U → R.carrier ⊆ K → ∃ R' : IMRep (univ : Set (Euclid P)) n, R'.carrier = R.carrier ∧ R'.mult = R.mult ∧ R'.orient = R.orient
subproblems.natural_proof:
Source: the parent-supplied proof of cbrcs_cutoff_extension, step 11 (first half: R̂ is an IMRep in ℝ^P).

1. (Data.) Define R′ with carrier M := R.carrier, multiplicity θ := R.mult and orientation ξ := R.orient. Then R′.carrier = R.carrier, R′.mult = R.mult and R′.orient = R.orient hold by construction.
2. (Fields not involving the domain.) The fields measurableSet_carrier (M is Borel), rectifiable (M is countably n-rectifiable), measurable_mult (θ measurable), mult_pos (θ(x) > 0 for x ∈ M), aestronglyMeasurable_orient (ξ is a.e. strongly measurable for Hⁿ⌞M) and orients (for Hⁿ-a.e. x ∈ M, ξ(x) is a unit orientation of an approximate tangent space of M at x) mention only M, θ, ξ and Hⁿ = μHE[n], not the domain; they are copied from the corresponding fields of R.
3. (carrier_subset.) M ⊆ ℝ^P = univ trivially.
4. (locallyIntegrable_mult.) Let K′ ⊆ ℝ^P be compact (the condition K′ ⊆ univ is automatic). Since M ⊆ K, every point of M ∩ K′ lies in M ∩ K, so M ∩ K′ ⊆ M ∩ K. The set lintegral is monotone in the set (lintegral_mono_set), hence ∫⁻_{M ∩ K′} θ dHⁿ ≤ ∫⁻_{M ∩ K} θ dHⁿ. The right side is ≠ ∞ by the field locallyIntegrable_mult of R applied to K, which is compact and contained in U. Therefore ∫⁻_{M ∩ K′} θ dHⁿ ≠ ∞ (ne_top_of_le_ne_top).
5. (Conclusion.) Steps 1–4 supply all fields of IMRep univ n, so R′ is an integer multiplicity triple in ℝ^P with the same carrier, multiplicity and orientation as R. ∎

Lean note (verified to compile as one theorem): refine ⟨{ carrier := R.carrier, mult := R.mult, orient := R.orient, measurableSet_carrier := R.measurableSet_carrier, carrier_subset := subset_univ _, rectifiable := R.rectifiable, measurable_mult := R.measurable_mult, mult_pos := R.mult_pos, locallyIntegrable_mult := ?_, aestronglyMeasurable_orient := R.aestronglyMeasurable_orient, orients := R.orients }, rfl, rfl, rfl⟩, then ne_top_of_le_ne_top (R.locallyIntegrable_mult K hK hKU) (lintegral_mono_set hsub).
proof_key_steps: Copy carrier, multiplicity, orientation and every field of R that does not mention the domain.
The carrier is contained in ℝ^P trivially.
For compact K′, ∫_{M∩K′} θ dHⁿ ≤ ∫_{M∩K} θ dHⁿ < ∞ because M ⊆ K and K is a compact subset of U.

subproblems.title: A current vanishing on forms supported away from a compact set has compact support inside it
subproblems.statement: Let P, n ∈ ℕ, let U ⊆ ℝ^P be open, K ⊆ U compact, and F ∈ 𝒟_n(U) with F(ω) = 0 for every ω ∈ 𝒟^n(U) whose topological support is disjoint from K. Then spt F ⊆ K and spt F is compact. Here spt F = U ∖ Z(F) (GeometricCurrentOn.support), Z(F) being the union of all open W with closure(W) compact, closure(W) ⊆ U and F(ω) = 0 for every ω ∈ 𝒟^n(U) with tsupport ω ⊆ W.
subproblems.lean_statement: ∀ (P n : ℕ) (U K : Set (Euclid P)) (F : GeometricCurrentOn U n), IsOpen U → IsCompact K → K ⊆ U → (∀ ω : TestFormOn U n, Disjoint (tsupport (ω : DifferentialForm (Euclid P) n)) K → F ω = 0) → F.support ⊆ K ∧ IsCompact F.support
subproblems.natural_proof:
Reused comparator-accepted declaration rsd_cmr_support_subset_of_vanish (DAG node root.regular_set_dense-a1.constant_multiplicity_reduction-a1.support_of_vanishing-a1, accepted with a candidate commit) with byte-identical frozen type; its accepted natural proof is reproduced verbatim below. The parent cbrcs_cutoff_extension applies it with U := ℝ^P (univ, open) to F := E X and uses the first conjunct.

Source: parent proof, step 6(f) (“For y ∈ U ∖ K choose s > 0 with B̄_s(y) ⊆ U ∖ K … S − T vanishes on all forms supported in B_{s/2}(y), whose closure is compact and contained in U, so y ∉ spt(S − T). Thus spt(S − T) ⊆ K. Being relatively closed in U and contained in the compact K ⊆ U, spt(S − T) is compact”), isolated for an arbitrary current F; the parent applies it to F = S − T.

1. Points of U ∖ K are not in spt F. Let y ∈ U ∖ K. Since U is open and K is closed (compact), U ∖ K is open (IsOpen.sdiff), so there is s > 0 with B_s(y) ⊆ U ∖ K. Put W := B_{s/2}(y).
 (a) W is open and y ∈ W.
 (b) closure(W) ⊆ B̄_{s/2}(y) ⊆ B_s(y) ⊆ U ∖ K ⊆ U.
 (c) closure(W) is compact, as a closed subset of the compact closed ball B̄_{s/2}(y) (ℝ^P is proper).
 (d) If ω ∈ 𝒟^n(U) and tsupport ω ⊆ W, then tsupport ω ⊆ B_s(y) ⊆ U ∖ K is disjoint from K, so F(ω) = 0.
 By (a)-(d), W is one of the sets whose union is Z(F), so y ∈ Z(F) and y ∉ spt F.

2. spt F ⊆ K. By definition spt F ⊆ U, and by step 1 no point of U ∖ K lies in spt F.

3. Compactness. From spt F = U ∖ Z(F), spt F ⊆ K and K ⊆ U, we get spt F = K ∖ Z(F). Z(F) is open, as a union of open sets (isOpen_zeroRegion). So K ∖ Z(F) is a closed subset of the compact set K, hence compact (IsCompact.diff). ∎
proof_key_steps: For y ∈ U ∖ K, a ball B_{s/2}(y) with closure in U ∖ K is a relatively compact zero set of F, so y ∉ spt F.
Hence spt F ⊆ K, and spt F = K ∖ Z(F) is compact because Z(F) is open.
